# WavWiz

> Free, MIT-licensed multi-zone music system built around Windows. Optional Linux/Docker server (amd64, plus arm64 for Raspberry Pi since 0.7.0; arm64 not yet verified on real Pi hardware). No cloud account, no telemetry. Public beta.

Current public beta: **0.7.2**, released 21 November 2026. Windows installer: `WavWiz-Setup-0.7.2.exe` (full SHA-256 and file size pending publication of the GitHub release; the installer checksum starts with `B889C5FE` and ends with `214D`). Linux server tarballs: `wavwiz-server-0.7.2-linux-x64.tar.gz` and `wavwiz-server-0.7.2-linux-arm64.tar.gz` (pending the same release). Docker image tags `0.7.2` and `latest` are intended to be multi-arch `linux/amd64` + `linux/arm64` once published to Docker Hub. The arm64 build is intended for Raspberry Pi 4/5 but has not been verified on real Raspberry Pi hardware. New in 0.7.2: live sources (stream a PC's own sound or its microphone to any zone, in Real time or Sync with WavWiz), Announce from the Windows Player or a phone, mic gain up to +24 dB with a limiter, phone drag onto Now Playing, and a Gradient zone edge light. Not yet: AirPlay receiver on Linux / Raspberry Pi, and calibration for AirPlay and Cast speakers (both planned for the next version).

WavWiz runs a server on an always-on Windows PC (or on Linux, bare or in Docker, on 64-bit Intel/AMD; a 64-bit ARM build for Raspberry Pi 4/5 has been available since 0.7.0 and is not yet verified on real Pi hardware) and plays through Windows WavWiz Players or any modern browser on phones, tablets, Macs and Linux PCs. Zones play different music or link for sync, with per-speaker delay, volume and EQ. Sources: local folders, NAS shares, internet radio, Subsonic/Navidrome, and (since 0.7.2) a PC's live sound or microphone. AirPlay in from iPhone, iPad and Mac; AirPlay 1 speaker output; AirPlay 2 output is experimental and off by default. Google Cast speaker output has been available since 0.7.0 and is still in testing. HomePod and Apple TV are unsupported. AirPlay 1 password speakers, FairPlay, and AirPlay 2 PIN devices are not covered. The Docker image (0.7.2 and latest, once published) is a multi-arch amd64 + arm64 server: no AirPlay receiver yet, no AirPlay 2 output; since 0.7.0 it can play through the host sound card. Calibrate speakers does not support AirPlay or Cast speakers yet. Home Assistant control is via REST plus an optional custom component (not on HACS). Spotify Connect is unofficial, off by default, and needs Premium. AI coding agents wrote the code; the developer designs and tests.
